read.market_reaction: Q2 (July 22, 2026): "Shares fell 6.5% intraday then recovered after hours." The note says nothing about peer or sector moves around that print, so whether the decline was company-specific is not stated. Q1 (April 23): "Q1 2026 (April 23) triggered a sector wide plunge alongside IBM as investors read AI as a threat rather than a driver." As of the 2026-09-04 screen pull, "Price 145.59 USD on 2026-09-04", "-30% from 52 week high, -42% from all time high", forward P/E 29.1 against a four-year median of 123.4. The only estimate-revision figure in the file is "Next fiscal year EPS estimate moved -0.4% in 90 days.", measured to that same 2026-09-04 pull; the note gives no revision series and does not break the change out by print, so it cannot be attributed to Q2 or Q1 individually.
not_determinable: Anything management actually said at either print. The file has no transcript, prepared remarks, Q&A, or executive quotation — CEO, CFO, management, call, and transcript all return zero matches — so nothing can be identified as addressed, deflected, or dodged. This is why the dodged list is empty rather than populated.

Q2 2026 EPS, total revenue, gross or operating margin, free cash flow, or share count. The earnings section reports only subscription revenue, its growth rate, and the full-year subscription guidance range. The financial table is annual and stops at FY2025.

Whether Q2 beat or missed. No consensus figure for the quarter appears; the word consensus does not occur in the file, and the only 'beats' reference is inside a source URL slug, not in the note's own text.
The prior full-year subscription guidance range, so the magnitude of the raise is unknown, along with any implied Q3 split, constant-currency assumption, or guidance for margin, EPS, or cash flow.

RPO, cRPO, or backlog. These words appear nowhere in the file. The note also says nothing about what this company customarily discloses, so their absence here cannot be read as an omission by management rather than by the note's author.

Federal or public-sector exposure, geographic mix, vertical mix, customer counts, net revenue retention, churn, and renewal rates. None of these terms appear, and the note gives no basis for judging whether any of them is material here.

Whether the $1 billion AI annual contract value and the ninefold rise in agentic deployments were Q2 disclosures. Both sit in the undated 'Business quality' section — 'ServiceNow AI passed $1 billion of annual contract value with agentic deployments up ninefold in nine months.' — and the note never ties them to a reporting period, an as-of date, or the July 22 print.

Which margin line is under pressure from AI compute costs, and by how much. The note asserts pressure without naming a line or a figure. The annual table shows FY2025 gross margin of 77.5% against FY2024's 79.2%, while operating margin rose from 12.4% to 13.7%; the note does not connect either move to AI costs.

Two of the three thesis killers cannot be tested from this file. Subscription growth under 18% is checkable (reported growth is 24.5%). An operating margin guidance cut is not, because no margin guidance is given. A large customer publicly replacing ServiceNow with an agent platform is not, because the note reports nothing about customer wins, losses, or defections in either direction.

Any price path between the July 22 print and the 2026-09-04 screen pull, including where the stock settled after the intraday drop and after-hours recovery, and how far it sits from the $110 price trigger or the $115 to $135 buy zone at any date other than 2026-09-04.

Balance-sheet or capital-return actions around the quarter. Buyback, repurchase, and dividend appear nowhere in the file; net cash is given only as an annual series through FY2025 (-3.88 USD bn, negative = net cash).
Any pre-FY2022 history or quarterly series for the financials. The note states its own limit: 'Four fiscal years is all the source provides.'

read.standing_caveat: A research note is already a summary, so its silence is usually the author compressing rather than management evading. Every entry under 'not addressed' below should be read at the confidence it states, and none of them is evidence about what was said on the call, because no transcript was available. See NOTES.md.

thesis.why_on_the_list: Compounder bucket, rank 63. Subscription revenue growing 24.5%, forward P/E 29 vs a 123 median, 42% off its high. Still the most expensive name on the shortlist on earnings.
thesis.business_quality: Platform moat inside the enterprise: once workflows are built on it they rarely leave. ServiceNow AI passed $1 billion of annual contract value with agentic deployments up ninefold in nine months. Margins are under some pressure from AI compute costs.
thesis.verdict: Buy on pullback only. Buy zone $115 to $135. Not in the initial portfolio; ADBE and ADSK carry the software exposure at better prices. Conviction 3 of 5.

risks.bear_case: Agents that live in the model layer make the workflow layer a commodity: why route a ticket through ServiceNow when the assistant resolves it? Seat based pricing shrinks as agents replace people. Margins are already compressing from AI costs, and at 29x there is no valuation cushion if growth slips to the teens.
killers: subscription growth under 18%, operating margin guidance cut, or a large customer publicly replacing it with an agent platform

own_history.caveat: The median is taken at four fiscal year ends, so it is a four-point median. That is a thin basis for 'cheap against its own history' and it says nothing about whether the old multiple was deserved.

drawdown.caveat: The all-time high is the highest closing price; the 52-week high is an intraday high. They are not on the same basis, and the drawdown from the all-time high is therefore understated.

price_basis.note: The drawdowns and the multiple-versus-median above were computed inside the price screen from its own last close, which is not quite the price shown at the top of this page: the two come from different passes of the pipeline and differ by a fraction of a percent. Neither is wrong; they are just not the same number.

written_view.text: At $145.59 and 29x forward, growth of 22% gives a PEG near 1.3, fair rather than cheap. Three year view: bear 22x is roughly $150, flat; base 30x on 20% compounded EPS is about $250; bull 38x is about $320.
